In Willoughby Heights, Langley, the 55+ homes you can buy are Willow Park Estates (strata). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is retirement residence or care. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Willoughby Heights
Willow Park Estates (also written Willowpark Estates) — 6467 197 St (Willoughby Heights)

The one complex in Willoughby verified as 55+ by name in listing and building sources. A current listing (Oct 2026) calls it a "pet-friendly 55+ community" close to shopping and transit, with pets recorded as cats OK, dogs OK, number limit two, with restrictions; the building source records the strata restrictions as age restrictions, pets allowed with restrictions, and rentals not allowed — on rentals. An earlier listing states the occupancy form as "at least one owner must be 55" and a maximum of 2 occupants per unit, and lists a clubhouse and recreation centre among the amenities. Confirm the registered bylaw wording, the occupant cap and the pet rule in the strata documents before writing.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Willoughby Heights (not for sale)

items.t: Langley Seniors Village — 20363 65 Ave (Willoughby): A registered assisted-living residence (BC Assisted Living Registry, class SN, operator Langley Seniors Village 3 LLP). Fraser Health describes it as owned and operated by Retirement Concepts with 64 publicly subsidized assisted-living units in studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom suites, with lunch and dinner included daily, weekly light housekeeping, and cats and small dogs allowed where the resident can care for them. Assisted living is accessed through Fraser Health assessment for the subsidized units — it is not a purchase and not a general market rental.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Willoughby Heights

items.t: Willoughby Heights is the board's sub-area name; the Township's official planning name for the area is "Willoughby." The Willoughby Community Plan Area in Bylaw No. 6201 is bordered by the City of Surrey municipal boundary to the southwest, Highway 1 to the north, the Trans Mountain Pipeline ridgeline / Lower Mainland Regional Park and 68 Avenue to the south, and 216 Street and the Willowbrook Connector to the east.
Main streets: 200 Street, 208 Street, 80 Avenue (Willoughby Way), 72 Avenue, 76 Avenue, 84 Avenue and 86 Avenue; Highway 1 runs along the north boundary with interchanges at 200, 208 and 216 Streets.
Hubs: Langley Events Centre, 7888 200 Street, and the Carvolth Exchange area at 200 Street and Highway 1; Muriel Arnason Library is at 130 - 20338 65 Avenue.

Schools physically in Willoughby include Donna Gabriel Robins Elementary, 7844 204B Street, and Lynn Fripps Elementary, 21020 83 Avenue; Township statements also name Willoughby Elementary, Yorkson Creek Middle School and R.E. Mountain Secondary as Willoughby schools. Catchments are address-based through the SD35 School Locator.
There is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in Willoughby.

Health: Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway, is the Fraser Health community hospital for Langley; the Langley Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 202 - 20434 64th Avenue, on the wider 64 Avenue corridor south of the plan area.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Willoughby Heights

parts.t: The rules that apply across the Township of Langley (zoning, suites, strata, land and taxes) are on one page:
buying a home in the Township of Langley: the rules

items.t: Township zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 2500: governs Willoughby. Its Residential Compact Lot Zone R-CL (s. 403) is the area's compact-lot pattern: under s. 403.7, R-CL lots run from a minimum lot area of 220 m² to a maximum of 464.5 m², with minimum frontage of 11 m for front-loaded lots and 8.2 m for rear-loaded lots. Neither Willow Park Estates nor Highgate Terrace is an R-CL product — both predate the compact-lot build-out (1987 and 1990).
Plans: Bylaws No. 6201, 6202 and 6203 replaced the Willoughby Community Plan and created the Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan and the Gordon Neighbourhood Plan.

Assisted living is a regulated care product, not a tenancy product a buyer shops for like a condo: Langley Seniors Village is registered with BC's Assisted Living Registry (class SN), and Fraser Health states its 64 units are publicly subsidized — access runs through Fraser Health, not through a listing.

blocks.text: BC’s 55+ rules (age bylaws, who may live in a unit, exemptions and rentals) apply in every strata and are on the BC 55+ strata rules page.
Good to know about Willoughby Heights

items.t: Willoughby's 55+ stock predates Willoughby. Willow Park Estates (1987) and Highgate Terrace (1990) were built decades before the Transit Corridor and Town Centre build-out that defines the area today — a buyer expecting "new Willoughby" form in a 55+ complex will not find it; the age-restricted product here is 1980s–1990 low-rise at the area's southwest edge, near Willowbrook.

The name is spelled two ways in the records. Listings and the building source alternate between "Willow Park Estates" and "Willowpark Estates" for the same 6467 197 St complex — a name-only search under one spelling will miss listings filed under the other.

One building source gives both 22 units and, through the strata-plan listings at the address, two plans totalling a 58-unit figure — and it records an age restriction with no age attached. Until the strata plan and registered bylaws are pulled, neither a unit count nor a "55+" label for this building should be published as fact.

The richest 55+ townhouse supply near Willoughby is not in Willoughby. Walnut Grove, directly across Highway 1, holds Churchill Park (147 units), Spencer Green (97 units), Chartwell Green and Chelsea Green, all marketed as 55+ — search engines and listing portals routinely blur the two sub-areas because they share the 208 Street / 88 Avenue corridor.

Willoughby's one in-area seniors institution is care, not housing product. Langley Seniors Village at 20363 65 Ave sits on the 65 Avenue corridor inside the plan area, but its 64 units are publicly subsidized assisted living — it will appear in every "Willoughby seniors housing" search while offering nothing a buyer can purchase.

The plan update changed what will be built next door, not the age rules. Bylaws 6201–6203 replaced the Willoughby Community Plan and created the Transit Corridor Plan and the Gordon Neighbourhood Plan — a buyer at the older 197 St / 64 Ave complexes is buying beside a corridor planned for high-density general-market growth, with no age-restricted project named in the plan material checked.

blocks.text: Sources for what’s nearby each building

faq.q: What 55+ homes can I actually buy in Willoughby?
faq.a: One complex: Willow Park Estates, 6467 197 St — a 64-unit townhouse complex built in 1987, described in current listings as a 55+ community. Highgate Terrace at 19645 64 Ave is age-restricted on its building record. Everything else attached in Willoughby is general-market.

faq.q: Do both of us have to be 55 at Willow Park Estates?
faq.a: A listing states the rule as "at least one owner must be 55" with a maximum of 2 occupants, and provincial strata rules in any case exempt a younger spouse or partner of a resident who meets the age requirement. Get the registered bylaw wording before writing — the listing form and the bylaw form are not the same document.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Willow Park Estates unit?
faq.a: The building source records "rentals not allowed," but long-term strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void province-wide since Nov 24, 2022. The tenant still has to satisfy the 55+ bylaw or an exemption, and short-term rentals can still be restricted. Confirm the current position from the bylaws and Form B.

faq.q: Are pets allowed at Willow Park Estates?
faq.a: Current listing data records cats OK and dogs OK, number limit two, with restrictions; an earlier listing recorded one cat or one dog to a maximum weight. The registered pet bylaw governs; check it in the strata documents.

faq.q: Is Langley Seniors Village something I can buy or rent on the open market?
faq.a: No. It is a registered assisted-living residence at 20363 65 Ave with 64 publicly subsidized assisted-living units, operated by Retirement Concepts; subsidized assisted living is accessed through Fraser Health assessment.

faq.q: Is Chartwell Langley Gardens in Willoughby?
faq.a: No — it is at 8888 202 St in Walnut Grove, north of Highway 1, and Willoughby's plan area is bounded by Highway 1 to the north. It is a continuum-of-care rental residence (independent living, assisted living, memory living and long-term care), not a Willoughby purchase option.
